name: a-module-that-may-grow-past-what-the-host-admits-is-refused
note: The pair to 34. There the module asks for memory a one-page host cannot supply; here its minimum fits and its declared maximum does not, so the host would be admitting a module that has said it will grow to four pages. §4.1 refuses both the same way and for the same reason — a host MUST NOT grant less than the module declared — so capping this one at instantiation is not an option a conforming host has. Every host runs this scenario, because the ceiling is loader configuration and the loader is shared code. A module declaring no maximum has said nothing to refuse and is the engine's to bound (§4.1), which is why there is no scenario for that case: what a guest sees there is `memory.grow` answering -1, which reaches the ABI only as `eio_alloc` returning 0 — 17_allocator_refuses' path (§9.5).
